html:
SMTO-EXE-0193 — This PDF needs a password

GUID: edf4a71b-1a60-5796-83d2-7f4b0c88de38
Slug: pdf-encrypted-password-required
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: pdf

What happened

  • This PDF is locked with a password, so SMTO can't read or change what is inside it. SMTO can still show basic details, like that it is locked, but nothing else was done.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store, choose "PDF password" in the menu next to New, select New, type the PDF's password into the password field on the Value tab, and select Save. The Parameter Store keeps the password private so it never appears in the conversation.
  2. In your message to SMTO, type @ and choose the PDF password entry you just saved, then ask for the PDF step again. Mentioning the entry gives SMTO permission to use that password for this PDF only.
  3. Don't type or paste the password itself into the conversation. Passwords in messages can be seen in the conversation history, while the saved entry stays hidden.

What success looks like

  • SMTO opens the PDF and finishes the step without asking for a password.

If it still fails

  • If SMTO says the password is wrong, check it by opening the PDF in a PDF reader, then update the saved entry. If it still fails, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, but never include the password.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The PDF is encrypted and the empty-password attempt did not unlock it for an operation that needs content access, and no password_ref was supplied.

What this means

  • The PDF is encrypted and empty-password decryption did not unlock it for an operation requiring content access; info can report the locked document without opening its content. PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.

Why this can happen

  • The PDF is encrypted and empty-password decryption did not unlock it for an operation requiring content access; info can report the locked document without opening its content.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect locked/encrypted metadata and the intended operation, then select an accepted typed private password reference.

How to fix it

  • Create a Parameter Store entry from the pdf_password template holding the password, have the user explicitly accept it by mentioning it in the request, and pass only password_ref ("@entry-key") to the PDF tool. Never put the password in ordinary tool arguments; a wrong password returns password_invalid instead.
  • Accept an existing private pdf_password Parameter Store reference and pass only password_ref. Never put a password in ordinary tool arguments.

Retry and execution caution

  • Accept an existing private pdf_password Parameter Store reference and pass only password_ref. Never put a password in ordinary tool arguments.

How to verify the fix

  • The accepted private credential unlocks the document with the rights needed for that operation.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
